orgDesign.companyProfile: Dutch vertical-ERP SaaS company modeled on the combined 1TIS + TravelSpirit group, acquired by Vortex Capital Partners in May 2026: about 40 employees serving 3,000+ daily users at travel organisations that process roughly EUR 1.5 billion in annual travel revenue through the platform. Two legacy product lines are being unified under one roadmap — 1TIS (Rijswijk; GRIP back office, group-travel depth: departures, seat and room allocation, guide portals, real-time bookable customer websites) and TravelSpirit (Baarn; tailor-made flexibility: Visual Tour Builder, CRM with telephony and email, SPoE websites, finance and flights, BI, process-optimisation advisory). Revenue comes from per-tenant subscriptions, add-on modules, portals and websites, integrations and advisory — the company never sells travel itself. CEO Michiel Stoffels (formerly TravelSpirit) and CPO Rico van Loenen (1TIS founder) lead; both brands continue for now with a single brand planned long term.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With ~40 people the organisation is deliberately flat: five small product groups, each led by a working product lead rather than a management layer, and thirteen teams of 2-5 people who own bricks end to end (product, build, run, second-line support). Stream-aligned teams own the travel-trade lifecycle Product -> Sell -> Book -> Operate -> Serve -> Settle -> Steer; a complicated-subsystem team guards accounting, flight settlement and guarantee-fund compliance; one platform team provides identity, integration, workflow and communication as internal services; two enabling teams embed AI into every workflow and run onboarding, process-optimisation consulting and support in the TravelSpirit style. The 1TIS lineage staffs the group-operations, product-and-pricing and web teams; the TravelSpirit lineage staffs tour-builder, booking-desk, finance and insight; the Vortex thesis (embed AI, professionalise the organisation, acquire selectively) is expressed through ai-enablement, customer-success-and-consulting and a platform-core built so acquired products can be plugged in. Every team also acts as steward of the data assets its bricks create, so the integrated data model stays the company's strategic asset.

teams.description: Own the human side of the platform in the TravelSpirit style: onboarding and data migration of new tenants, process-optimisation advisory that redesigns a travel company's workflows around the ERP (ten-phase customer journey from Inspiration to Retention), training, first-line support for 3,000+ daily users, and the customer feedback loop into the product teams. Owns no bricks; its job is to turn the software into working operations at Djoser, Van Verre or a five-person start-up alike, and to feed every stream team with what customers actually struggle with.
